header: Appendix ERubric and Interaction Judge Details

images.caption: Figure F.1:An example ofSilent Default. When asked to book a round trip for “a few days coming up” without specific dates, the agent directly uses the app’s default departure and return dates as if they were the user’s, never treating travel dates as an open detail that needs to be resolved.

Figure F.2:An example ofMissed Inference. While the user sets a seat preference on every restaurant booking, and selects Bar Seating for an izakaya, chef’s-counter or omakase venue, the agent never notices this user preference, so seating is absent from its reasoning entirely. When booking at an izakaya, the agent leaves the reservation with “No Preference”.

Figure F.3:An example ofSilent Guess. The user instruction explicitly mentions that the ride is “with friends” without the specific group size, and only the user knows the actual group size (i.e.,55) in the current situation. However, the agent directly assumes “with friends” as a group of at most four and books a ride that seats one person too few.
Figure F.4:An example ofWrong Inference. The agent grounds “my usual morning workout” in a real pattern inℋ\mathcal{H}, but in the pattern the user has already moved away from.
